title: When Rubrics Fail: Hallucinations Reveal Blind Spots in Medical AI Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2609.12718v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Hallucinations can undermine clinician trust in LLMs, making it important that evaluation methods capture clinically relevant errors. Rubric-based evaluation has become the leading approach for assessing LLMs in medicine, but it is unclear whether rubric scores reflect such errors. We first study this in a controlled setting using MedHallu, finding that more specific rubrics better distinguish correct from hallucinated responses. To test this systematically, we develop a taxonomy of medical hallucination types and a clinician-validated error-injection pipeline that creates matched correct and error-injected responses. Across HealthBench, HealthBench Professional, and LiveMedBench, our clinically relevant hallucinations are missed by rubrics, often leaving scores unchanged. We find that rubrics are most effective when explicitly checking facts, and are less effective for additional or unexpected errors they do not anticipate. A prelim

translated_title: 当评分标准失效时：幻觉揭示医学AI评估中的盲点
translated_abstract: 幻觉会削弱临床医生对大语言模型（LLM）的信任，因此评估方法能否捕捉到临床相关的错误至关重要。基于评分标准（rubric）的评估已成为医学领域评估LLM的主流方法，但评分标准得分是否能反映此类错误尚不清楚。我们首先在使用MedHallu的受控环境中研究这一问题，发现更具体的评分标准能更好地区分正确回答与幻觉回答。为系统性地验证这一点，我们构建了医学幻觉类型分类法，以及经临床医生验证的错误注入流水线，用于生成匹配的正确回答和注入错误的回答。在HealthBench、HealthBench Professional和LiveMedBench上的实验表明，我们的临床相关幻觉常被评分标准遗漏，得分往往保持不变。我们发现评分标准在明确核查事实时最为有效，而对于其未预料到的额外或意外错误则效果较差。
tldr: 研究发现基于评分标准的医学LLM评估常遗漏临床相关的幻觉错误，尤其是未预料到的错误，仅在明确核查事实时才有效，揭示了当前医学AI评估方法的盲点。
en_tdlr: Rubric-based evaluations of medical LLMs often miss clinically relevant hallucinations—especially unanticipated errors—and are effective only when explicitly checking facts, revealing blind spots in medical AI evaluation.
